transcript.note: Whole-grid assignment, not a nudge of the rank-snapping control. Two design rules. (1) orderFlip guard by construction: col is a weakly monotone function of gx and row a weakly monotone function of gy, so no unambiguous E/W or N/S pair can invert. Ties are free, which is the entire budget I spend on straightness. (2) H/V comes only from merging *rank-adjacent* points into a shared column or row, never from reordering. Bands used: col 33 = Bukit Panjang/Beauty World/Haw Par Villa/Woodlands North/Woodlands/Buona Vista/Botanic Gardens (the whole west-central spine: DTL NW branch + TEL Woodlands + CCL west); col 44 = Orchard/Mayflower/Newton/Outram Park (NSL+TEL central); col 47 = Tanjong Pagar/52/Clarke Quay/57/Dhoby Ghaut; col 52 = Marina Bay/53/Raffles Place/City Hall/51/Bugis/55 as one unbroken NSL-EWL spine giving 6 verticals; col 60 = Paya Lebar/MacPherson/Serangoon; col 68 = Tanjong Katong/Bayshore/Buangkok/Punggol Coast/Bedok North; col 73 = Tanah Merah/Tampines/Pasir Ris. Rows: row 0 = HarbourFront/Marina Bay/Marina South Pier; row 8 = Outram Park/Maxwell/52/50/53/Bayfront/Haw Par Villa, a 5-segment horizontal chain along the EWL+TEL waterfront; row 17 = Fort Canning/57/City Hall/Promenade; row 27 = Buona Vista/Napier/Orchard/Little India/55; row 32 = Botanic Gardens/Stevens/Newton/Paya Lebar/Bayshore; row 38 = Tuas Link/Pioneer/Jurong East/Caldecott/MacPherson/Bedok North/Tanah Merah/Expo; row 46 = Marymount/Bishan/Serangoon. (3) Every merge was checked so no shared line ever runs over a third vertex sitting on it — that is why Marymount/Caldecott sit at col 45 rather than joining col 44 (a col-44 Mayflower-Caldecott vertical would have run straight through Marymount), and why Changi Airport stays off Expo's column (Tampines East is between them).
